newsitem.title: CHINA: China cotton trader says official forecast too low.
newsitem.headline: China cotton trader says official forecast too low.

text.p: China's cotton output in the 1996-97 season was expected to slip but forecasts by the State Statistics Bureau were too low, an official of the China Textile Cotton Import and Export Corp said on Monday.

The bureau had said the cotton harvest was expected to plummet to around 3.5 million tonnes in 1996, a drop of more than 1.0 million tonnes compared with 1995, due to a 533,000 hectare reduction in the area under cotton.
An official of the state cotton trader said the bureau forecast was too low, but admitted that the bureau figure was the most authoritative.
"According to our information, China's cotton output will drop this year, but not so low," the official told Reuters. He declined further comment.
Analysts have said a lack of price incentives and rising domestic cotton stocks have led many farmers to switch to other crops.
Last Wednesday, the International Cotton Advisory Committee (ICAC) lowered its forecast for China's 1996/97 cotton output to 3.7 million tonnes from 4.1 million tonnes.
China's 1995/96 cotton crop was 4.8 million tonnes, according to the ICAC.
